artists.biography:
Isobel Campbell (born on 27 April 1976) is a Scottish singer, cellist and composer in the indie and rock genres. She was born in Glasgow. She is a former member of the Scottish indie pop band Belle & Sebastian, but left the group to pursue a solo career, first as The Gentle Waves, and later under her own name. Recently, she has collaborated with singer Mark Lanegan on three albums.
Isobel Campbell's music has been described as either indie pop, chamber pop or singer-songwriter. Regardless of genre, Campbell makes gentle and sombre music, often using classical instruments and her bright, slightly nasal voice with bittersweet and ironic songwriting.

perplexity.description:
Isobel Campbell’s 2024 album Bow To Love, released on Cooking Vinyl, is a reflective and nuanced work that blends elements of pop, folk, and country. The album features a soft-spun yet sharp-edged sound, marked by Campbell’s signature cello arrangements and delicate vocals. Lyrically, Bow To Love grapples with contemporary crises and personal introspection, offering both diagnosis and a sense of hope for moving forward from tense and conflicted times. The musical style is rooted in folk traditions but incorporates subtle pop sensibilities and occasional world music textures, creating an intimate and atmospheric listening experience.

Bow To Love stands as Campbell’s sixth solo studio album and marks a significant point in her discography, following her acclaimed collaborations with Mark Lanegan and her earlier work with Belle & Sebastian. The album continues her evolution as a solo artist, showcasing her ability to merge traditional folk influences with modern songwriting. It was well-received by critics, with outlets such as musicOMH and The Skinny highlighting its emotional depth and musical craftsmanship. The album’s original release in 2024 was accompanied by a bonus disc of French translations for the CD edition and limited vinyl pressings, underscoring its special place in Campbell’s catalog.
